BACKGROUND In the elderly, exercise training is a safe and effective intervention to reduce the risk for cardiovascular disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
exercise training in patients with HFpEF improves exercise capacity, functional capacity, quality of life and reduces hospitalization.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the exercise responses of elderly patients who have diastolic heart failure are comparable to those of elderly patients who’ve systolic heart failure.
exercise training is safe and effective for patients with diastole heart failure (HF) and systolic HF, but there are some differences between the groups.
the results of this study suggest that older individuals with diastolic HF may be at a higher risk of developing systolic dysfunction than older individuals with systolic HF.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a new approach to measure the exercise capacity in patients with diastole and systole failure.
we found a significant association between the exercise responses of elderly patients (≥65 years) with diastolic (HFpEF) or systolic heart failure (HFrEF) and the presence of HF symptoms.
we have identified a new mechanism for the development of heart failure.
